title: Stable-Limit Simultaneous Bands for Event-Study ATT Paths under Weak Overlap
banked_reason: D0.5.G: delivered tier=incremental below novelty_target=field; paper_score_ceiling 6.2 < 7.4; not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The delivered theorem requires a globally exact quadratic propensity in a known uniform scalar coordinate and a public total-variation boundary rate; uniformizing a covariate alone does not justify that joint restriction.
The n^{-1/3} width characterizes the specified untrimmed procedure, without establishing optimal inference for the smooth ATT class or an advantage over boundary extrapolation.

No reproducible finite-sample comparison establishes the procedure’s practical value, and the CAPS connection supplies neither a validated quadratic-tail model nor a delivered application, constraining the projected paper score to 6.2.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a uniform feasible bivariate 3/2-stable limit, paired angular-measure consistency, and honest simultaneous bands for the specified exact-quadratic two-period class. Review exposed and repaired zero-mark totality and scalar-projection degeneracy; an untargeted open-family calibration counterexample was removed without changing the positive theorem chain. Independent math and decision reviews passed with no findings, but the general referee rated the scoped result incremental, below the field floor; broader propensity tails, optimality, and applied validation remain open. No Lean formalization was started.
tldr: Conditional parallel trends identifies the two-coordinate ATT path, while a common rare comparison unit can dominate both untrimmed doubly robust scores. Over the bespoke exact-quadratic class \(\mathcal P\), the total cross-fitted estimator has a uniform \(n^{1/3}\) bivariate \(3/2\)-stable limit, the paired rare-control procedure consistently estimates its angular measure, and compensated-Poisson calibration gives an honest simultaneous \(90\%\) rectangle even near line support. These positive feasible-band results are not claimed for the broader classes in the anchor papers.
gap: Published weak-overlap theory provides scalar IPW and doubly robust stable limits, while published DiD procedures provide Gaussian simultaneous bands after regularity or trimming. Generic multivariate stable approximation and angular-measure estimation do not establish feasible causal calibration with learned paired residuals.
fill: The project identifies the causal angular measure, poses the complete nonparametric learned-score transfer as the central open problem, proves a line-support-uniform maximum-CDF modulus, and combines these pieces into a total simulated simultaneous band with a dependence-blind failure theorem.
